source_ranges: include/mulib-json.h (construction, access, mutation, bounded parsing and stringify ownership)
preconditions: Destroy only an owned root, never a borrowed/transferred child.
Input strings/keys are live UTF-8 with the specified extent. NULL for length-delimited inputs is valid only at length zero; SIZE_MAX lengths are invalid.
Exclude concurrent mutation/destruction and concurrent LC_NUMERIC changes during numeric parse/serialization.
postconditions: Failed append/set retains caller ownership and leaves existing members intact.
Successful set to an already-installed identical value is a no-op; other replacement destroys the old child.
Accessors borrow from the containing tree. Missing pointer and a non-NULL JSON-null value are distinct.
Stringify's text is independent malloc-owned storage released with free, not mulib_json_destroy.
Parse initializes optional diagnostics on success/failure; diagnostic messages are static and partial trees/captures are cleaned on failure, including object-key lookup work exhaustion.
unlowered: Conditional ownership and same-value alias exception.
Borrow invalidation for replaced subtrees and multi-level owner relationships.
Length-delimited strings may contain NUL, unlike the current On1x string ABI.

preconditions: Initialize fresh/freed struct storage; init overwrites but does not free old storage.
Use nonzero stride and valid length/capacity/data invariants. Element/output storage must cover stride bytes.
Elements are trivially copied bytes. Resource-bearing pointers have no automatic clone/drop behavior.
postconditions: Reserve/push return 1/0 and preserve existing state on failed growth.
Push can copy a live element across realloc by recording/rebasing its offset.
Growth can invalidate every buffer borrow; pop/clear also invalidate removed logical elements.
Pop with NULL output discards bytes; failure does not initialize an output object.
Clear does not free capacity or nested pointees. Free releases buffer storage, retains stride and permits reuse; it does not free the struct.
unlowered: Borrow regions tied to realloc and logical vector length.
Stride-based buffer extents are not ordinary pointer+length argument pairs.
Owned element types cannot be admitted by raw memcpy.

preconditions: Every descriptor's transitive child/literal/bitmap/reference-slot/user/label referent must outlive each run.
Do not mutate reference slots or grammar storage concurrently with a run.
Predicate callbacks must be pure and may run repeatedly under backtracking; no unregister function exists for these non-owning value descriptors.
Run output storage is fresh or result_free'd, and result_free only accepts initialized/zeroed storage.
postconditions: Constructors return C structs by value; they neither allocate nor copy referenced buffers.
Run returns 1 match, 0 mismatch, -1 fatal/invalid/limit/allocation. Failure commits no captures and retains no capture allocation.
Successful result owns captures, not source bytes or diagnostic labels. result_free resets storage for reuse.
Run is prefix parsing; only an explicit end descriptor enforces whole-input parsing.
Bounded run additionally charges literal comparisons; zero max_work selects 16000000.
unlowered: ReturnKind borrow can describe a borrow-bearing value, but field-sensitive aggregate lifetime lowering is absent.
satisfy/named have multiple borrowed field origins; these functions deliberately retain unknown/unsafe metadata.
Indirect grammar callbacks are not explicit function-pointer parameters to run. Their effects remain unknown until separately proved.
Owned MULIB_IMPL_PARSER grammar/AST APIs are outside this combinator-only profile; MANIFEST extra macros are not enabled implicitly.

source_ranges: include/mulib-mune.h: public declarations, runtime C API, native callback path, GC roots and standard-library implementations
manual/mulib-mune.md: ownership, limits, standard-library behavior, modes and module formats
tests/test_mune_runtime.c, tests/test_mune_runtime_alloc.c and tools/check_mune_runtime.py: source-pinned execution/allocation/differential evidence
on1x/tests/fixtures/mune_semantics.c: separate-TU archive/C ABI ownership and Lua-library acceptance
preconditions: Do not confuse mulib_mune_t (legacy transactional numeric environment), mulib_mune_chunk_t, mulib_mune_state_t and mulib_mune_result_t ownership/destructors.

Tagged values are real C enum/union aggregates. Scalars copy; object fields borrow live same-state GC storage. Never fabricate tags, dereference stale object pointers, mix states or narrow double/size_t to i64 by guessing.

Keep object values in a global/table or owned result root before execution/collection. A copied tagged struct, string pointer, userdata byte pointer or upvalue identity does not itself keep an object alive.

Execution/call result slots start as NULL; success transfers an owned root. Destroy results before their state. Callback argument arrays, state and output builders are borrowed and must not be destroyed by the callback.

Serialize access to each state/chunk/environment. Do not destroy or select modes on an executing state. Native callbacks may reenter mulib_mune_call and execute on a coroutine's C11 worker, not necessarily the initiating host thread.

Retained native callback code and external user context must outlive their closures; conservatively keep them until state destruction. The recorded unregister endpoint is whole-state destruction, not a nonexistent per-closure unregister API. function_owner can instead retain state-owned userdata through GC tracing.

AOT entry arrays, production-name strings and native program/execute pointers must outlive all closures retaining the generated chunk. Writer callbacks/context are synchronous borrows; do not mutate their input chunk or throw across the C callback ABI.

Source/binary input pointers denote their exact extents; NULL is permitted only where documented at zero length/count. Names/paths are NUL-terminated. Runtime strings are arbitrary binary bytes and are not On1x NUL-free strings.

Lua execution is not a sandbox: io/os/debug/package, native modules, finalizers and callbacks may do I/O, change host locale, exit the process or suspend. Application-wide locale/environment/standard streams require separate synchronization. JIT is host-dependent.
postconditions: Legacy eval commits environment/output together only on success. Runtime run/call/metamethod APIs preserve preceding Lua side effects on failure; diagnostic and value out-parameter validity are separate conditions.

Parse owns copied source/AST and never executes it. Parse diagnostic text is static. Execution diagnostic text borrows state until its next execution; some invalid-argument branches leave diagnostics unchanged.

Constructors/accessors return state-borrowing tagged outputs, not independently destroyable GC objects. make_userdata returns zeroed state-owned byte storage and a traced user-value table, not malloc ownership.
result_destroy removes the root/list but does not directly free its contained GC objects. chunk_destroy consumes one reference; retained closures can keep the AST and compiler caches alive.

Raw global/table/uservalue APIs and table_next do not invoke Lua. get_index/get_field/set_index/set_field can invoke arbitrary metamethods, while rooting their inputs; failed getters preserve C output storage.

The updated library keeps package registry aliases and retained package closures, installs four searchers, handles independent Mune dump/load metadata/stripping and uses xoshiro256** random generation. Native module ABI and bytecode containers remain independent of PUC Lua.

load_bundle verifies checked source/helper images before registration and does not execute modules; a failure while updating _PRELOAD can leave earlier registrations. Writer callback failures can leave partially written C/bundle output.

Explicit active_optional_macros enables MULIB_IMPL_PARSER only for Mune's complete runtime recipe; Parsec's standalone combinator profile remains narrow. The archive contains one kernel implementation TU.
unlowered: GC root regions, cross-state identity, aggregate enum/union ABI and nested borrowed object fields require field-sensitive ownership/ABI lowering.
Conditional owned result outputs, runtime-vs-static diagnostic lifetimes, reference-counted chunks and finalizer resurrection are not ordinary scalar error/ownership protocols.
Retained/reentrant coroutine-thread callbacks, AOT function-pointer arrays and arbitrary Lua/native/OS effects need reviewed adapters and usage/effect proofs.
All 52 functions remain raw/unreviewed metadata and are ineligible for the current signed-integer/void scalar emitter; passing Gate B is not safe export.

source_ranges: include/detail/mulib-webscan.h (iterative scanner and explicit work accounting), include/mulib-json.h (bounded JSON tree construction)
library/elvis/*.elvs and on1x/tests/mulib/elvi-scrape.{on1x,c} (trusted declarative providers, offline On1x acceptance)
preconditions: Programs originate from compile/load and remain unmodified during use. All C pointers and capacities denote live, correctly sized, nonoverlapping storage.

Load only trusted provider files. TLS callbacks report negotiated authenticated state, enforce public resolved addresses and never fabricate verification. Generic fetch transports must not implicitly follow redirects.
Buffer is initialized; callback/context lifetimes cover synchronous operations. No concurrent mutation of shared outputs or callback context.
postconditions: Compile/url/parse preserve outputs on failure except compile diagnostics; search may report status on a later failure. Zero parse results is success.
An empty query selects the validated provider homepage. A nonempty query expands into a literal, exact-host HTTPS template with complete percent escapes and no fragment.
HTTPS transport preserves caller outputs on failure; successful append may reallocate body. Every created session is closed and temporary allocations are freed.
HTTPS prohibition and tighter fetch limits are preserved. No redirect, pagination or rate-limit retry is performed.

Scanner work exhaustion and allocation failures preserve all caller results/count. HTML stages output and ignores opaque/inert containers; JSON validates the tree and result schema before emitting any output.
Extraction uses the first href attribute (quoted or unquoted) and preserves the UTF-8 title prefix across text spans when clipping.

Google targets are unambiguous/nonempty and stop before wrapper fragments; invalid numeric URL entities and request fragments reject. Exact-byte destination duplicates are removed without changing URL path/query meaning.
HTTPS response metadata rejects duplicate type/encoding and unsupported content encodings; bounded fixed/chunked/EOF framing and partial reads/writes are tested separately from extraction.
Explicit provider-fixture selection retains the source-pinned recipe, evidence inputs and required exports; no optional owned parser or safe status is inferred.
unlowered: Indirect callbacks and transitive context effects remain unknown; no safe export.
Struct array extents, fixed character arrays, conditional diagnostic/status outputs, and peer verification trust cannot be inferred from extraction.
